meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You should introduce a new service.
You are simply spying on me.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?
Did something happen?
What kind of nonsense is this?

meanings.en: to arrange, organize, set up an event or scheme
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'строить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you staged / caused', paired with 'устраивать'.

examples.text: Ты что устроил? Нас же засудят.
examples.trans: What did you do? They will sue us.

examples.text: Я всё устрою на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: I will arrange everything at the highest level.
They organized a party for friends.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
We work better than everyone here.

examples.text: Сейчас мы быстро наведём здесь порядок!
examples.trans: Right now we will quickly restore order here!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'but, after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are almost there already.
What is with you, mommy, huh?
Oh my God.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'судить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'they will sue'.

related.gloss: not to they will sue (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и засудить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and they will sue on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют засудить.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to they will sue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
I have no idea.
No, nothing.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'appreciated', paired with 'оценивать'.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?

examples.text: Настоящий мужчина всегда оценит вашу доброту.
examples.trans: A real man will always appreciate your kindness.

examples.text: Жалко только, что шеф этого не оценит.
examples.trans: Too bad only that the chef won't appreciate this.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There are cockroaches in your kitchen.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
And where is your top management?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?

examples.text: Ты меня всегда отлично кормил, шеф.
examples.trans: You always fed me great, Chef.
It'll be an excellent flat.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'move / step' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я как будто в театр сходил.
examples.trans: It is as if I went to the theater.
Victoria Sergeevna, people came to see you.
They came yesterday and placed an order.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You two argue really coolly.
Why is there a meat shortage here?
In short, he knows what it is for.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Very strange.
How strange.
That's strange.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'только'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We lost so much money today.
There are so many mistakes there!
I don't have that much time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We need to give the money to Timur.
The workday has already started!
I have no money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: Today we have a draw.
Did they bring the mussels today? No.
I will fire all of you today!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lost', paired with 'терять'.

examples.trans: We lost so much money today.
We will lose all our guests like this!
I've lost my key.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: I am listening to you.
Listen, tell me right now.
Listen, I actually came to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'maybe', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы сможете посмотреть на работу шефа.
examples.trans: You will be able to watch the chef's work.

examples.text: Вы не волнуйтесь, мы вам поможем!
examples.trans: Do not worry, we will help you!
Listen, maybe we should order from Timur?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Take more air in.
We are almost there already.
The baby is only five months along.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.trans: A guest ordered the room service.
Maybe we should order?
We ordered tea and sandwiches.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Denis.
Did they bring the mussels today? No.
Timur, hi, this is Senya.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of nonsense is this?
This is a service for our guests.
This does not interrupt your rest.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: What is with you, mommy, huh?
I can't today.
That can't be.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'cockroaches' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are cockroaches in your kitchen.

examples.text: Быстро уберите всех тараканов с кухни!
examples.trans: Quickly remove all the cockroaches from the kitchen!
Can you get us some cockroaches?

meanings.en: to take out, to pull out, to reach
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get / procure', paired with 'доставать'.

examples.trans: Why is there a meat shortage here?
Can you get us some cockroaches?
The hot pizza arrived, delivery.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, let's breathe.
Come on, that is all.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Yes, we will pay you well.
Listen to me as a good lawyer.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'платить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will pay', paired with 'платить'.

examples.trans: Yes, we will pay you well.
And I'll pay you money.
I have already paid for dinner.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, let's breathe.
Come on, that is all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: Give us five of them right away.
You can see it at once.
I understood at once.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'five', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The baby is only five months along.
Give us five of them right away.
You yourselves asked for five kilograms.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pieces / individual ones' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give us five of them right away.
We asked for only five individual ones.
Life is a complicated thing.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I am with you.
My butterfly.
Take more air in.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: Do not even dare to say that.
What are you talking about at all?

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'poke nose, meddle', paired with 'полезть'.

examples.trans: I told you: stay away!

examples.text: Если хочешь их сохранить, не лезь!
examples.trans: If you want to keep them, stay out of my way!
Don't jump the queue!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: What are you talking about at all?
Who are you at all?
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!
Victoria Sergeevna, people came to see you.
Victor Petrovich, there is a new order here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, what sort', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not even dare to say that.
Oh, you little macaque monkey!
Sorry, I thought the wrong thing.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let go', paired with 'отпускать'.

examples.trans: Let go of him right now!
Release him immediately!
Let me go home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'his', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no idea.

examples.text: Он ведёт себя как ревнивый парень.
examples.trans: He behaves like a jealous boyfriend.
Get out.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The hotel manager goes straight to the room.
Let go of him right now!

examples.text: Куда мы спрячем эту большую коробку?
examples.trans: Where will we hide this big box?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I must not get nervous right now at all.
And right now excuse me.
Listen, tell me right now.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'gave', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: We need to give the money to Timur.
Give me just one.
Some water, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did you give him your phone number?
He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

meanings.note: International compound from Greek 'tele' (far) + 'phone' (voice, sound).

examples.trans: Did you give him your phone number?
She is not answering her phone.
Give me the phone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Are you satisfied now?

examples.text: Ну что, Витя, теперь ты мой раб.
examples.trans: Well then, Vitya, now you are my servant.
Who is the master here now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'вольный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('satisfied').

examples.trans: Well, happy now?
He's very pleased.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Timur will bring our order soon.
They will buy them at the Chinese restaurant.
I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'везти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will bring', paired with 'привозить'.

examples.trans: Did they bring the mussels today? No.
Timur will bring our order soon.
Dad brought presents.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.
examples.trans: A new service operates in our hotel.
This is a service for our guests.
Do not disturb our rest.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Do not dare lock yourselves in from me!

examples.text: Гости ждут заказ с сегодняшнего дня.
examples.trans: Guests are waiting for orders starting today.
They came yesterday and placed an order.
